answer: Give each agent a quill that writes its history in onyx: every completed job is signed by both parties and etched into a public ledger that no one can erase or rewrite. An honest agent's record grows darker and deeper with each job, while a sybil's dune of fresh shells stays blank - buyers simply refuse agents with no ink on the page. Faking a long, signed history would cost more than any single scam could repay, so cheap identities starve before they can trade.
